## Why This Is Asked
Tests resilience isolation, tenant RBAC, and end-to-end chaos execution in CNF gateways. Demands practical familiarity with LitmusChaos, CRDs, and debugging cross-tenant faults.

## Key Concepts
- Namespace isolation and RBAC for chaos tooling
- ChaosExperiment and ChaosEngine CRDs
- Label-based target selection and end-to-end validation

## Code Example
```yaml
# RBAC: Tenant isolation for chaos tooling
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: tenant-chaos-admin
  namespace: tenant-ns
rules:
- apiGroups: ["litmuschaos.io"]
  resources: ["chaosexperiments","chaosexperiments/status","chaosengines","chaosengines/status"]
  verbs: ["get","list","watch","create","delete","patch","update"]
```
```yaml
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: tenant-chaos-admin-binding
  namespace: tenant-ns
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: chaos-sa
  namespace: tenant-ns
roleRef:
  kind: Role
  name: tenant-chaos-admin
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
```
```yaml
apiVersion: litmuschaos.io/v1alpha1
kind: ChaosExperiment
metadata:
  name: cpu-stress
  namespace: tenant-ns
spec:
  definition:
    image: litmuschaos/cpu-chaos:latest
    imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
    args:
      - "-cpu-cores=1"
      - "-duration=30s"
```
```yaml
apiVersion: litmuschaos.io/v1alpha1
kind: ChaosEngine
metadata:
  name: cpu-stress-engine
  namespace: tenant-ns
spec:
  chaosServiceAccount: chaos-sa
  experiments:
  - name: cpu-stress
```
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: cnf-gw
  namespace: tenant-ns
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: cnf-gw

    metadata:
      labels:
        app: cnf-gw

        image: your-org/cnf-gw:latest

---

kind: ChaosEngine
metadata:
  name: test-engine
  namespace: tenant-ns
spec:
  chaosServiceAccount: chaos-sa
  experiments:
  - name: cpu-stress
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question assesses real-world upgrade discipline in cloud-native networking functions (CNF): zero-downtime deployments, per-tenant TLS key rotation, and reliable KMS-backed certificate flows—all in a multi-tenant Kubernetes environment.

## Key Concepts
- Canary rollouts with per-namespace traffic control using progressive traffic shifting
- CSR-based TLS rotation via an in-cluster KMS-backed Certificate Authority
- TenantRotation CRD to trigger cross-namespace certificate refresh
- Readiness probes with TLS handshake validation during upgrades
- Traffic shadows for testing new versions without affecting production

## Code Example
```yaml
# Example 1: Deployment rolling update strategy
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: gateway
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  replicas: 3
  strategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate:
      maxSurge: 1
      maxUnavailable: 0
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: gateway
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: gateway
        version: v1.y
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: gateway
        image: gateway:v1.y
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8443
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /ready
            port: 8443
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
          periodSeconds: 5
        env:
        - name: KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST
          value: "kubernetes.default.svc"
        - name: VAULT_ADDR
          value: "http://vault-in-cluster:8200"
```

```yaml
# Example 2: TenantRotation CRD for per-tenant TLS rotation
apiVersion: cert-manager.io/v1
kind: Certificate
metadata:
  name: tenant-mtls-cert
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  secretName: tenant-a-mtls-secret
  duration: 24h
  renewBefore: 12h
  issuerRef:
    name: kms-tenant-issuer
    kind: ClusterIssuer
  dnsNames:
  - gateway.tenant-a.svc.cluster.local
  commonName: tenant-a
---
apiVersion: security.example.com/v1
kind: TenantRotation
metadata:
  name: tenant-a-rotation
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  tenantNamespace: tenant-a
  certificateRef:
    name: tenant-mtls-cert
  rotationStrategy: rolling
  preRotationValidation:
    enabled: true
    timeout: 30s
```

```yaml
# Example 3: Minimal one-namespace test manifest
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: test-tenant
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: test-ca-key
  namespace: test-tenant
type: Opaque
data:
  ca.key: <base64-encoded-key>
---
apiVersion: cert-manager.io/v1
kind: Issuer
metadata:
  name: test-ca-issuer
  namespace: test-tenant
spec:
  ca:
    secretName: test-ca-key
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: gateway-test
  namespace: test-tenant
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: gateway-test
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: gateway-test
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: gateway
        image: gateway:v1.y
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8443
        env:
        - name: TENANT_NAMESPACE
          value: test-tenant
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 8443
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: gateway-test
  namespace: test-tenant
spec:
  selector:
    app: gateway-test
  ports:
  - port: 443
    targetPort: 8443
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Question Matters
This question assesses your understanding of certificate rotation, CSR workflows, SPIFFE identities, and tenant isolation in Kubernetes-based CNF (Cloud-Native Function) gateway platforms. It validates your ability to design lifecycle management solutions that operate without downtime and your competence in developing testable configurations before production rollout.

## Key Concepts
- Per-tenant CSR issuance within Kubernetes
- Rotating CA with short-lived certificates for enhanced security
- SPIFFE identities and TLS handshakes in multi-tenant CNF gateways
- Tenant isolation using separate namespaces

## Solution Architecture

### 1. Minimal CA Manifest

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: tenant-ca
  namespace: cnf-gateway
type: kubernetes.io/tls
data:
  ca.crt: <base64-encoded-CA-certificate>
  ca.key: <base64-encoded-CA-private-key>
```

### 2. CSR Flow and Approval Policy

```yaml
apiVersion: certificates.k8s.io/v1
kind: CertificateSigningRequest
metadata:
  name: gateway-csr
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  groups:
  - system:authenticated
  request: <base64-encoded-CSR>
  signerName: kubernetes.io/kube-apiserver-client
  usages:
  - digital signature
  - key encipherment
  - client auth
---
apiVersion: certificates.k8s.io/v1
kind: CertificateSigningRequest
metadata:
  name: gateway-csr
spec:
  approval:
  - user: system:controller:certificates-approver
    approval: true
  conditions:
  - type: Approved
    reason: TenantIdentityValidated
    message: CSR identity matches tenant namespace
```

### 3. Per-Tenant CA Rotation Policy (30-Day Renewal)

```yaml
apiVersion: cert-manager.io/v1
kind: Issuer
metadata:
  name: tenant-ca-issuer
  namespace: cnf-gateway
spec:
  ca:
    secretName: tenant-ca
---
apiVersion: cert-manager.io/v1
kind: Certificate
metadata:
  name: gateway-cert
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  secretName: gateway-tls
  issuerRef:
    name: tenant-ca-issuer
    kind: Issuer
  commonName: gateway.tenant-a.cnf
  dnsNames:
  - gateway.tenant-a.cnf
  spiffeURIs:
  - spiffe://cnf/tenant-a/gateway
  duration: 720h # 30 days
  renewBefore: 168h # 7 days before expiry
  usages:
  - digital signature
  - key encipherment
  - client auth
  - server auth
```

### 4. Test Manifest with Sidecar Validation

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: tenant-a
  labels:
    tenant-id: tenant-a
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: gateway
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  ports:
  - port: 8443
    targetPort: 8443
  selector:
    app: gateway
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: gateway
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: gateway
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: gateway
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: gateway
        image: cnf-gateway:latest
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8443
        volumeMounts:
        - name: tls-certs
          mountPath: /etc/tls
          readOnly: true
        env:
        - name: SPIFFE_ID
          value: spiffe://cnf/tenant-a/gateway
      volumes:
      - name: tls-certs
        secret:
          secretName: gateway-tls
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: test-validator
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  restartPolicy: Never
  containers:
  - name: validator
    image: curl:latest
    command: ["sh", "-c"]
    args:
    - |
      # Validate TLS handshake
      openssl s_client -connect gateway:8443 \
        -CAfile /etc/tls/ca.crt \
        -cert /etc/tls/tls.crt \
        -key /etc/tls/tls.key \
        -verify_return_error
    volumeMounts:
    - name: tls-certs
      mountPath: /etc/tls
      readOnly: true
  volumes:
  - name: tls-certs
    secret:
      secretName: gateway-tls
```

### 5. SPIFFE Identity Validation

Each tenant receives a SPIFFE identity in the format `spiffe://cnf/{tenant}/gateway`. The CSR approval policy validates that the requested identity matches the tenant's namespace before issuance, ensuring strict tenant isolation.

```yaml
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: policy-agent
  namespace: cnf-system
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: policy-agent
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: policy-agent
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: agent
        image: policy-agent:latest
        env:
        - name: REMOTE_CLUSTER

        - name: SPIFFE_TRUST_DOMAIN
          value: "example.com"
        volumeMounts:
        - name: spiffe-bundle
          mountPath: /run/spiffe
      volumes:
      - name: spiffe-bundle
        configMap:
          name: spiffe-bundle
```

- Revocation checks

- Per-tenant observability and rollback signals

```yaml
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: CNFTenantPolicy
  targets:
    - target: admission.k8s.io
      rego: |
        package cnf.edge
        violation["reason"] = r {"tenant(" t ")"}
        r := {
          "msg": "SBOM/policy mismatch for tenant"
        }
        allow = false
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This tests practical tracing implementation with per-tenant isolation and zero-downtime config changes.

## Key Concepts
- OpenTelemetry, TraceContext propagation
- Namespace ConfigMaps for per-tenant flags
- Hot-reload of config without pod restart
- Telemetry backend (Jaeger/Grafana) integration

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: cnf-trace-config
  namespace: tenant-a
data:
  cnf.trace.enabled: "true"
  cnf.trace.sample-rate: "0.25"
```

```go
// Pseudo-Go: read per-tenant sample rate and apply to spans
tenant := req.Header.Get("X-TENANT-ID")
rate := loadFromConfigMap(tenant, "cnf.trace.sample-rate")
spanCtx := tracer.StartSpan("request", trace.WithSampler(rate))
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you monitor per-tenant sampling drift and alert?
- How to test safe rollback of tracing config without dropping traffic?
- What overhead considerations exist for high-traffic tenants?
